lead: Most people use AI as a question machine: open it, ask, copy, close. It's like hiring a brilliant consultant and wiping their memory every morning. In personal life, cultivation is cheap: three or four text files and twenty minutes a week.
objetivo: start personal cultivation with one function, an About me file, three rules and the 20-minute weekly review.

aprende.t: Pick one function at a time

hero_alt: Person at the kitchen table in the morning writing in a notebook next to the laptop.

secoes.sub: Three files and one habit. Click each part.

nos.detalhe: One role at a time: writing reviewer, study coach, spending analyst, weekly planner. Not "does everything".
One page: who you are, life stage, goals for the year, limits on time, money and health, values, and what you hate. One good page is worth more than twenty dumped in.
E.g.: "never decide for me on money and health; give me options", "be direct, no praise", "answer in English".
Preferences it has discovered, what has already been tried, what worked. You delete whatever is no longer true.
Read the memory, write three lines in the failure log, fix it in the file, and clean up the memory. This is what turns the chat into cultivation.

secoes.volta: The week's correction becomes a rule or context, and next week starts from there
secoes.legenda: Someone who does the review for eight weeks ends up with an AI that doesn't look like anyone else's.

secoes.titulo: Five gardens that pay off fast

texto: Role: an advisor who doesn't decide. Context: your criteria and past decisions with their outcomes. Rule: always present the opposing option.
Over time, it remembers your own patterns: "last time you picked the cheapest and regretted it".
Role: spending analyst. Tool: a spreadsheet exported from your bank. Rule: never move money, only show it.
Spending categories and patterns show up that you had never seen.
Role: tutor. Examples: one explanation that "clicked" and one that didn't. Assessment: it asks, you answer, it notes where you get stuck.
The memory becomes the map of your gaps.
Role: an editor with your voice. Examples: five of your texts. Rule: don't change the tone, only clarity.
After a month, the first draft comes out almost ready. Health and routine follow the same logic: suggest and ask your doctor, never prescribe.

secoes.sub: Copy into SOBRE-MIM.md, REGRAS.md, and the review note.

blocos.conteudo:
# About me — <name>          reviewed on <date>

Who I am: 
This year's goals: 1)  2)  3) 
Constraints (time, money, health): 
How I like to work: direct, no praise, English, short lists
What I hate: 
Decisions already made (don't reopen):

# Rules — role: <e.g.: writing reviewer>

1. Never decide for me on money or health; present options.
2. Be direct, no praise.
3. Answer in English.

# Never
- third-party data or passwords in this file

## Review — week of <date>
1. I read MEMORIA.md: what did it note that's new?
2. Three lines in FALHAS.md: date | what went wrong | smallest fix | was context, a rule, or an example missing?
3. I fixed it IN THE FILE (not in the conversation): 
4. I deleted from memory what is no longer true:

texto: Write About me (one page). Pick a role. Set three rules.
Use it every day in the same role. Gather five good examples. Start the failure log.
First real weekly review. Edit the context and rules. Create the Memory file.
Add one tool (calendar or spreadsheet). Measure: time saved and how many times you redid things. Decide whether to open a second role.

exercicios.texto: Write SOBRE-MIM.md and REGRAS.md with a single role. The personal kit has the files with a fictional example.
exercicios.pronto: About me fits on one page, the role is written in one sentence, and there are exactly three rules.

exercicios.texto: Use the AI in the same role for one week, loading the files at the start. At the end, do the review using the template above.
exercicios.pronto: FALHAS.md has at least three lines, and at least one of them turned into a change in a file (rule, context, or example).

perguntas.p: You've explained for the third time that you want answers in short bullet points. What do you do?
opcoes: Write a rule in the file
perguntas.explica: If you've explained the same thing three times, a rule is missing. Fixing it in the conversation disappears in the next session.

perguntas.p: What's the right size for About me?
perguntas.explica: Too much context becomes clutter. One good page is worth more than twenty dumped in.

perguntas.p: In the "spending analyst" role, which rule is essential?
opcoes: Never move money, only show it
perguntas.explica: The AI proposes, you decide, especially on money and health. Delegating judgment is the first trap.

perguntas.p: What goes into the context file deserves care because...
opcoes: it goes to the model provider
it gets too heavy for the computer
perguntas.explica: Privacy: what goes into the context goes to the provider. Think before you write third-party data or secrets.

itens.texto: One role at a time, never "does everything".
About me, rules, and memory, with the failure log alongside.
The fix goes into the file, not into the conversation.
